scope: P1/P2 development evidence only; no P3; no new optimizer run; no threshold retuning

checkpointTrajectory.interpretation: Selection-subset metrics were still strongest at the frozen final epoch, so this fold did not show a simple late-epoch collapse.
Selection-subset performance peaked before the end and declined by epoch 1000, indicating that simply extending the frozen epoch budget is not supported by this fold.

diagnosis.finding: V3 improved precision in both folds but reduced recall in both folds, especially P2->P1.
diagnosis.implication: The V3 activity/identity/temporal controls reduced some false-event behavior but likely became too conservative for part of the development population.

diagnosis.finding: The V3 gain is concentrated in P1->P2; P2->P1 F1 is essentially unchanged from V2 while completeness and recall are worse.
diagnosis.implication: The current V3 objective/decoder changes do not generalize symmetrically across the performer-disjoint folds.

diagnosis.finding: Scales remain the strongest content class while singlenotes remain the weakest in both folds.
diagnosis.implication: The remaining failure is not only temporal fragmentation; exact note/string identity for sparse single-note material remains a primary weakness.

diagnosis.finding: Macro F1 improved while macro completeness was essentially flat/slightly worse.
diagnosis.implication: The design improved event correctness more than temporal coverage, so a further decoder-only tightening is not supported.

diagnosis.finding: P2->P1 selection-subset metrics peak before epoch 1000 and then degrade.
diagnosis.implication: More epochs alone are not an evidence-based V4 hypothesis.

nextDiagnosticTask.purpose: Reconstruct exact V3 predictions and separate onset, activity false positive/false negative, string/fret confusion, pitch-correct wrong-string, fragmentation, end/duration, and per-content errors for each performer-disjoint fold, then compare directly with the frozen V2 decomposition.
